statement: For beta,a,b,Lambda>0 and 0<s<2, a real Gaussian displacement field modulo constants with covariance beta^-1 1_{0<|k|<=Lambda}(P_L/(a|k|^s)+P_T/(b|k|^2)) under Fourier measure d^2k/(2pi)^2 induces theta=curl(u)/2 with spectral density 1_{|k|<=Lambda}/(4 beta b). Its sixfold increment correlation tends to exp(-9 Lambda^2/(4 pi beta b))>0.
assumptions: Stipulated Gaussian comparison model only, not a Riesz Gibbs law or a particle bond observable.
Fixed positive stable shear coefficient b and fixed finite UV cutoff Lambda.
Spatial limit is taken at fixed beta,b,Lambda.
proof_or_counterexample: The curl multiplier kills P_L and contracts P_T to |k|^2/4. Its frequency density is integrable with variance Lambda^2/(16 pi beta b). Riemann-Lebesgue and the real Gaussian characteristic function give the stated limit.

remaining_gap: Independent constant review and microscopic transfer. This is not a proof or disproof of P0321.

statement: In the Gaussian model of P0321-G01, delta rho=-rho div u has frequency density rho^2 |k|^(2-s)/(beta a) for 0<|k|<=Lambda. This density sector is independent of b, whereas the orientational correlation limit depends on b.
assumptions: rho>0; exactly the Gaussian hypotheses in P0321-G01.
This is a continuous linearized density field, not a hyperuniformity theorem for a point process.
proof_or_counterexample: The divergence multiplier annihilates P_T and contracts P_L to rho^2 |k|^2, which divided by beta a |k|^s gives the formula. Density suppression therefore cannot alone identify the angular sector.

statement: For fixed nonzero G in the Gaussian model of P0321-G01, log E exp(iG dot [u(r)-u(0)])=-(|G|^2/(4 pi beta b)) log |r|+O(1) as |r| goes to infinity along a fixed direction. The model has algebraic positional rather than short-range positional correlations.
assumptions: All hypotheses of P0321-G01; 0<s<2 is required for the integrability of the longitudinal displacement spectrum.
G and the direction are fixed before the large-distance limit.
This observable is a Gaussian displacement characteristic function, not an established particle-density correlation.
proof_or_counterexample: The transverse angular integral gives pi |G|^2[1-J0(t)-cos(2alpha)J2(t)]. Integration against dt/t gives log |r|+O(1). The longitudinal integral converges, and the Gaussian characteristic function contributes one half of the variance.

statement: A single-valued C^1 displacement u on a neighborhood of a closed piecewise C^1 loop gamma has zero Burgers circulation: integral_gamma partial_j u_i dx_j=0 for every component i. Such a sector cannot itself represent a dislocation with nonzero circulation.
assumptions: u is single-valued and C^1 on a neighborhood containing the loop.
The loop is closed; repeated index j is summed.
No assertion is made that actual Riesz Gibbs states lie in this sector.
proof_or_counterexample: Parameterize gamma on [0,1]. The integrand is d/dt u_i(gamma(t)); integrate to u_i(gamma(1))-u_i(gamma(0))=0.

statement: If a stationary centered real Gaussian sequence X_n has nonzero finite variance sigma^2 and Cov(X_1,X_{1+h}) tends to zero, then for any finite rho>0, rho+X_n is negative for infinitely many n almost surely. Its one-point negative probability is Phi(-rho/sigma)>0.
assumptions: Joint Gaussianity and stationarity of the sequence.
0<sigma^2<infinity and covariance decay along the sequence.
rho is fixed and finite. No independence of all cells is assumed.
proof_or_counterexample: Bivariate Gaussian convergence gives covariance decay for negative-value indicators. The variance of their average tends to zero. Chebyshev excludes an all-nonnegative ray; stationarity and a countable union exclude only finitely many negatives.

remaining_gap: Independent mathematical review. Covariance decay is indispensable; constant Gaussian sequence is an explicit silent control.

statement: In the Gaussian comparison model of P0321-G01, the additive density rho+delta rho, delta rho=-rho div u, has variance rho^2 Lambda^(4-s)/(2 pi beta a (4-s)). It is negative infinitely often along an equally spaced ray almost surely and cannot have the exact one-point law of a finite nonnegative smoothing of a point configuration.
assumptions: beta,a,b,Lambda,rho>0; 0<s<2; the Gaussian model in ATTEMPT.md.
The proposed particle smoothing kernel is nonnegative and its point sum is finite.
This rejects exact additive-density identification only; it does not reject approximate fluctuation laws or the gas phase.
proof_or_counterexample: Radial integration of rho^2 |k|^(2-s)/(beta a) gives the variance; integrability gives covariance decay, so P0321-N01 applies. A nonnegative kernel yields a nonnegative particle smoothing, whereas a nondegenerate additive Gaussian density has a strictly positive negative tail.
